data.long_meaning: Atyanta means 'beyond' or 'extreme'. It is a powerful name derived from the Sanskrit language, often used in Hindu mythology to represent a limitless and boundless entity. The name Atyanta carries the meaning “Beyond, Extreme” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Atyanta usually hope their child will grow to embody beyond, extreme and live with faith, good character and purpose.

This name is often used to describe divine entities who transcend all limitations, including space, time, and human understanding. In Hindu mythology, gods and goddesses with the name Atyanta are believed to have limitless power, knowledge, and grace.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name "Atyanta" carries the deep meaning of the ultimate reality or truth that lies beyond our physical world. It reminds us of the infinite potential that exists within each of us and encourages us to reach beyond our current limitations to tap into the vastness of our inner selves. In Hindu philosophy, the pursuit of this ultimate reality, known as "Brahman," is the ultimate goal of life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Atyanta signifies the ultimate, the boundless, the endless. It embodies the limitless expanse of the divine, transcending all limitations and constraints.

historical_references.reference: Atyanta Samhata is a Jain text dating back to the 6th or 7th century AD. It is a collection of Jain canon consisting of various agamas and commentaries. The text is significant as it provides insight into the Jain doctrines during the medieval period.

Atyanta is also a name of a Hindu god, believed to be an incarnation of Lord Vishnu. According to the Bhagavata Purana, Lord Vishnu assumed the form of Atyanta to protect the people of the Haihayas during a war. The time period for this reference is not explicitly mentioned, but it is considered part of the Mahabharata epic tradition.
